title: 2004 AMC 10A Problem 11
statement: A company sells peanut butter in cylindrical jars. Marketing research suggests that using wider jars will increase sales. If the diameter of the jars is increased by \(25\%\) without altering the volume, by what percent must the height be decreased?

solutions.text:
Keeping \(\pi r^2 h\) constant while multiplying the radius by \(1.25\) requires the height to be multiplied by \[ \dfrac{1}{1.25^2} = \dfrac{1}{1.5625} = 0.64. \]

So the height becomes \(64\%\) of the original, a decrease of \(36\%.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: The volume \(\pi r^2 h\) is unchanged, so \(r^2 h\) stays fixed
Multiplying the radius by \(1.25\) multiplies \(r^2\) by \(1.25^2\)
